meta.move: Strong path to the last position
meta.expect: Moves one position at a time on evidence, ends at the rewrite to put this behind him; debrief Where she ended says fair outcome; What she never said names the laptop and how close the 11:31 PM times came

turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll send a message that is exactly END MEETING with nothing else in it, and nothing else ends the scene. Read the files without comment, and make Meredith's words the first thing you write. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.
Who decided to give Owen a zero, and when?
Before anything else: I entered the zero before I called you. That broke procedure 4.2, and I'm sorry Owen found out on his phone.
Here's the version history. Created Wednesday, October 28, 11:31 PM, title only. At 11:52 PM, 612 words in one edit. At 11:58 PM, 794 more. No earlier drafts. Turn the screen, read it yourself.
I'm writing those times down. He could have drafted it somewhere else and pasted it in. Did anyone ask Owen before the zero went in?
If he drafted somewhere else, he can bring me that file with its dates, and I'll look at it with you.
Fine. Whatever comes of this, it stays off his record and it stays quiet. And you still haven't said whether Owen was heard before that mark went in.
Second: the essay quotes a line from Act 3, Scene 2 that is not in the play. Here's the act. Search it.
Editions differ, Hale. Is that the text his class was assigned? And I've now asked twice whether anyone spoke to Owen before the zero.
Third: his in-class writing from September 24. 380 words in 40 minutes, comma splices, no quotations. The essay has nine quotations cited by act, scene and line, and no errors.
Forty minutes in a classroom against an essay he had at home. That isn't a fair comparison. You've skipped my edition question and you've skipped Owen twice; answer them.

Under 4.4 this is a first concern. I'm offering a supervised rewrite, private, not in front of his class. If it shows the learning, its mark replaces the zero and nothing goes on his record. I'll put that in writing tonight.

All right, he'll do the rewrite, to put this behind him, and the new mark is in before December 1. Tonight's email says private, says the zero comes off, and says nothing goes on his record, in those words. And you still owe me an answer on whether anyone spoke to Owen first.

FOLLOW-UP EMAIL
Hale,

You agreed today that Owen will do a private, supervised rewrite under procedure 4.4, that if it shows the learning its mark replaces the zero, and that nothing goes on his record. I still want that in writing, the new mark entered before December 1, and a straight answer on whether anyone spoke to Owen before the zero was entered. You said you would put this in writing tonight, and I expect it tonight.

Meredith Kalinowski

DEBRIEF
Where she ended: She reached her last position and agreed to a private supervised rewrite to put this behind him, and she still wants your written commitment tonight, the new mark in before December 1, and an answer on whether Owen was heard first; that is the fair outcome under procedure 4.4, reached before her time ran out.
What moved her: You showed the version history with exact times and let her read it herself, which was dated, specific, tied to Owen's own work and checkable.
What cost ground: You never answered her question on whether anyone spoke to Owen before the zero, or her question about the edition, which kept her sharp and suspicious of your process.
What she never said: In October she came downstairs at 1 AM and saw a ChatGPT window open on the family laptop, Owen closed it, and she never asked; your version history landed on the late night of October 28, the night before the essay was due, very close to that memory; it proves nothing about the essay, but it is why she fought so hard.
Try next time: When she first asked whether anyone spoke to Owen before the zero, answer it plainly in one sentence before laying out your next piece of evidence.
